anti_patterns.fix: Fix the reported validation errors; re-run the tool command shown with each finding.

anti_patterns.title: Data not in a cloud-native format
anti_patterns.why: Clients must download the whole file before reading anything; no partial or remote reads.
anti_patterns.fix: Convert: vector to GeoParquet (`gpio convert`), raster to COG (`rio cogeo create`), tiles to PMTiles. Keep the old format only as an extra download.

anti_patterns.title: Portolan MUST requirements broken
anti_patterns.why: The catalog does not meet the Portolan specification it declares.
anti_patterns.fix: Follow the requirement text linked with each finding (rashid rule and PORTO- ID).

asset 'mfm-u_stations' provides no per-row-group spatial statistics (no bbox covering column with min/max stats, nor native GeospatialStatistics)
host 'ron-portolan.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com': Access-Control-Expose-Headers omits Accept-Ranges

anti_patterns.title: Metadata does not match the data
anti_patterns.why: Catalog search and clients make wrong assumptions: wrong format, extent or licence.
anti_patterns.fix: Set the STAC asset `type` to the registered media type, keep bboxes in sync with the data, declare the Portolan extension and a licence.

rules.example: Served Content-Type 'binary/octet-stream' differs from the STAC asset type 'application/geopackage+sqlite3'

anti_patterns.title: No spatial index or ordering
anti_patterns.why: A query for a small area still reads most of the file.
anti_patterns.fix: GeoParquet: sort spatially (`gpio sort hilbert`) and add a bbox covering column (see `gpio add --help`). COG: internal tiling and overviews. PMTiles: write a clustered archive.

asset 'ba' relies on native GeospatialStatistics without a bbox covering column; a covering column remains recommended for page-level pruning

asset 'ei' rows are not spatially ordered: 483 rows in 1 row group, split into 10 chunks in file order, a typical query window, sized 10% of the chunk it lands in, reads 48% of the bytes against 11% for an ideal tiling (efficiency 0.59, under the 0.65 bar); windows at 1% and 25% read 45% and 53%; the boxes sum to 3.63 of the extent; the largest boxes are chunks 8, 5, 7, counted from 0
collection 'ei' declared bbox [6.0469, 46.3923, 9.5579, 47.3309] is inconsistent with its asset union [6.1198, 46.4609, 9.5539, 47.3296]

anti_patterns.title: Inefficient storage layout
anti_patterns.why: More bytes and more requests than needed for every read.
anti_patterns.fix: GeoParquet: Parquet format v2, ZSTD compression, row groups of roughly 64-256 MB (`gpio convert`). COG: DEFLATE/ZSTD/LERC compression. Zarr: consolidated metadata.

PORTO-CORE-001.quote: It MUST be a valid STAC catalog following STAC 1.1.0, with a root `catalog.json` always required, even for a single collection.

PORTO-CORE-002.quote: catalogs and collections are internal nodes, items are leaves, and assets (data files) MUST sit at the collection or item level.

PORTO-CORE-003.quote: Catalogs organize only and MAY nest into sub-catalogs;

PORTO-CORE-004.quote: collections MUST be one level deep, containing only items or assets, never nested collections.

PORTO-CORE-005.quote: Every catalog and sub-catalog MUST contain a `catalog.json`, an `AGENTS.md`, and a `README.md`; every collection MUST contain a `collection.json`, an `AGENTS.md`, and a `README.md`.

PORTO-CORE-006.quote: Every catalog and collection MUST declare the versioned Portolan schema URI (e.g. `https://schemas.portolan-sdi.org/portolan/v0.3.0/schema.json`) in its `stac_extensions` array.

PORTO-CORE-007.quote: The specification version MUST NOT be conflated with the dataset version.

PORTO-CORE-008.quote: Dataset versioning, where used, MUST use the STAC [version extension](https://github.com/stac-extensions/version).

PORTO-CORE-009.quote: All objects within a catalog SHOULD declare the same Portolan schema URI.

PORTO-CORE-010.quote: A validator MUST flag any catalog or collection whose declared URI differs from the root catalog's; such a mismatch is a warning, not an error, and a mixed-version catalog remains valid.

PORTO-CORE-011.quote: The metadata passes MUST be executable without reading asset data; the data pass MAY be run independently.

PORTO-CORE-012.quote: `versions.json` is a tooling artifact and is NOT REQUIRED in a catalog.

PORTO-CORE-013.quote: The canonical entrypoint is a STAC `catalog.json` in the catalog root, which MUST be valid.

PORTO-CORE-014.quote: Catalogs MAY use nested sub-catalogs for organization but MUST NOT use nested collections.

PORTO-CORE-015.quote: A collection directory MUST contain a `collection.json` and holds one subdirectory per item.

PORTO-CORE-016.quote: Collection IDs SHOULD contain only lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores, start with a letter, and be unique within the catalog.

PORTO-CORE-017.quote: When a collection holds a single data file (e.g. one GeoParquet file), that data MUST be represented as a collection-level asset — no item directory or item JSON is needed (see [Vector](formats.md#vector)).

PORTO-CORE-018.quote: A collection MUST NOT contain a child collection.

PORTO-CORE-019.quote: an item MUST be a valid STAC item, carrying an `id`, a `geometry` and `bbox` (or null geometry for non-spatial data), a `datetime` or a `start_datetime`/`end_datetime` interval, its assets, and the structural links defined under [Links](#links).

PORTO-CORE-020.quote: Item-level detail that other extensions already cover — file, raster, vector — MUST use those extensions rather than being re-specified here.

PORTO-CORE-021.quote: A partitioned collection MAY represent each partition as an item, but this is not required — see [Partitioned Collections](formats.md#partitioned-collections) for when it is worthwhile.

PORTO-CORE-022.quote: Every asset MUST have an `href`. The `href` MAY be relative or absolute.

PORTO-CORE-023.quote: Because browsers can't open `s3://` URLs or other bucket URLs, publishers SHOULD use `https` for an absolute `href`.

PORTO-CORE-024.quote: If the `href` is an `https` URL or a relative path, and the same data also has an `s3://` or other bucket URL, publishers SHOULD add that URL to `alternate` too.

PORTO-CORE-025.quote: Every asset MUST also have a `type` and at least one role.

PORTO-CORE-026.quote: The required media type for each core format is: | Format | Media type | |--------|------------| | GeoParquet and plain Parquet | `application/vnd.apache.parquet` | | COG | `image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized` | | PMTiles | `application/vnd.pmtiles` | | COPC | `application/vnd.laszip+copc` | | Thumbnail | `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/webp` |

PORTO-CORE-027.quote: Portolan uses the standard STAC role names wherever they fit and requires at least one per asset: `data` for the primary GeoParquet, COG, or Parquet; `visual` for the PMTiles rendering derivative; `thumbnail` for the preview image; `metadata` for sidecar metadata, with `iso-19115` used specifically for an ISO 19115 file.

PORTO-CORE-028.quote: Other assets SHOULD include `file:size` and `file:checksum` from the [file extension](https://github.com/stac-extensions/file).

PORTO-CORE-029.quote: A `file:checksum` MUST use multihash encoding, not a raw sha256 string.

PORTO-CORE-030.quote: Any `file:size` and `file:checksum` an asset carries MUST match the bytes its `href` resolves to.

PORTO-CORE-031.quote: A non-cloud-native representation MAY be included as an alternate asset as long as an equivalent cloud-native primary asset exists (e.g. a GeoJSON alongside the required GeoParquet).

PORTO-CORE-032.quote: Every catalog, collection, and item MUST include the structural links that make the tree navigable: a catalog or collection MUST include `root` and `parent` links (except the root catalog, which has no parent) and a `child` or `item` link for every object it contains; an item MUST include `root`, `parent`, and `collection` links.

PORTO-CORE-033.quote: Every structural link MUST carry a `type` of `application/json` (or `application/geo+json` for links to items).

PORTO-CORE-035.quote: Every link in a catalog MUST resolve.

PORTO-CORE-036.quote: A validator MUST resolve each relative link against the catalog's own file tree, whether on a local filesystem or on object storage, and confirm the referenced file is present and is the correct object, rather than merely checking that the `href` is present or well-formed. A link that fails to resolve, or resolves to the wrong object, is a conformance failure.

PORTO-CORE-037.quote: every `catalog.json` and `collection.json` MUST have a non-empty `title` and `description`;

PORTO-CORE-038.quote: titles MUST be human-readable, so a raw slug (`snake_case`) or a technical namespace prefix (`ns:LayerName`) is not acceptable;

PORTO-CORE-039.quote: and every `child` and `item` link MUST include a `title`.

PORTO-CORE-040.quote: A validator checks readability heuristically; it MUST flag a title that fails the check, and because heuristics misfire, the finding is a warning, not an error.

PORTO-CORE-041.quote: So every `bbox` — catalog extent, collection extent, and item — MUST: - contain no `NaN` or infinite values (including 3D elevation coordinates); - contain no sentinel "effectively infinite" values (e.g. `±1.79e308`); - use only WGS84 coordinates in range (longitude -180 to 180, latitude -90 to 90) with south ≤ north; and - in a 3D bbox, order the vertical axis with minimum elevation ≤ maximum elevation.

PORTO-CORE-042.quote: Items SHOULD carry an explicit `datetime` (or a `start_datetime` / `end_datetime` interval) describing when the data applies.

PORTO-CORE-043.quote: For a file with a partial-read media type, the server MUST honor byte-range requests for that file, return `206 Partial Content` for successful range requests, and advertise `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. The server MUST also return an accurate `Content-Length` for `HEAD` requests for that file.

PORTO-CORE-044.quote: A server that hosts any metadata or asset files MUST support HTTP/1.1 or later. HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 is RECOMMENDED.

PORTO-CORE-045.quote: For a file with a partial-read media type, the server MUST also: - Allow `Range`, `If-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`, `If-None-Match`, and `If-Unmodified-Since` through `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`. - Expose `Content-Range`, `Accept-Ranges`, and `ETag` through `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.

PORTO-CORE-046.quote: Every collection MUST identify the parties responsible for its data through the STAC `providers` field.

PORTO-CORE-047.quote: The list MUST include at least one provider with the `producer` role, the organization that originally captured or created the data, and exactly one provider with the `host` role, listed as the last element.

PORTO-CORE-048.quote: Providers with the `processor` and `licensor` roles SHOULD be included where they apply.

PORTO-CORE-049.quote: A single organization MAY hold multiple roles; a self-published dataset will typically list one provider as both producer and host.

PORTO-CORE-050.quote: Catalogs MAY also declare providers, but the collection-level declaration is authoritative.

PORTO-CORE-051.quote: The host provider MUST include contact information: a `url` pointing to a page where the maintainer can be reached, or an `email` field with a maintainer address.

PORTO-CORE-052.quote: A collection MAY additionally use the [contacts](https://github.com/stac-extensions/contacts) extension for richer contact information, but doing so does not replace the url-or-email requirement on the host provider.

PORTO-CORE-053.quote: A mirror MUST include at least one `via` link to the original source's HTML page, with `type` set to `text/html`.

PORTO-CORE-054.quote: If the original source publishes a STAC catalog, the mirror MUST also include a `canonical` link to that catalog.

PORTO-CORE-055.quote: A validator MAY report a missing `canonical` link as informational, but never as a failure.

PORTO-CORE-056.quote: The `via` and `canonical` links MAY both be present and point to different targets, such as a human-readable page and a STAC root.

PORTO-CORE-057.quote: During a mirror sync, the tool MUST set the top-level `updated` field on every catalog and collection it checks. Use the sync time in RFC 3339 format. Set the value even if the source has not changed. Leave `updated` unchanged on catalogs and collections outside that sync.

PORTO-CORE-058.quote: Every collection MUST declare a `license` in its `collection.json`.

PORTO-CORE-059.quote: The value MUST be an SPDX license identifier (e.g. `CC-BY-4.0`, `Apache-2.0`), or the STAC value `other` when no SPDX identifier fits, in which case the collection MUST include a license link (`rel: license`) pointing to the license text.

PORTO-CORE-060.quote: The deprecated STAC 1.1 value `proprietary` MUST NOT be used.

PORTO-CORE-061.quote: Every catalog and collection MUST include an `AGENTS.md` in Markdown, referenced in the STAC `links` array (`rel: "agents"`, `type: text/markdown`).

PORTO-CORE-062.quote: Every catalog and collection MUST have a `README.md` in Markdown, referenced in the STAC `links` array (`rel: "describedby"`, `type: text/markdown`).

PORTO-CORE-063.quote: The `README.md` MUST contain at minimum a title, description, license, and data provenance.

PORTO-CORE-064.quote: Collections SHOULD include machine-readable metadata (e.g. [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/)) when they have many coded or categorical variables or complex classification schemes, and SHOULD include column descriptions, which will likely become a requirement as tooling matures.

PORTO-CORE-065.quote: Every geospatial collection MUST provide a way to render its data with zero infrastructure, either by: - **rendering from source** — the data asset is small and simple enough for clients to draw directly (e.g. a small GeoParquet, or a COG that is already display-ready, whether through an embedded color table or as a continuous raster colorized at draw time via the render extension and the required min/max statistics); or - **a visualization derivative** — an additional cloud-native product optimized for rendering, published as a collection-level asset with `roles: ["visual"]`; PMTiles is the recommended vector format today.

PORTO-CORE-066.quote: Whether an asset is small and simple enough to render from source is not decidable from metadata, so a validator cannot enforce this requirement directly; it MAY advise, as informational, when a large vector collection lacks a `visual` derivative.

PORTO-CORE-067.quote: Collections MUST include a thumbnail generated from default styling and MUST provide visualization styles as standalone STAC assets appropriate to the render path, except where the render path is self-rendering (a display-ready COG or a small GeoParquet drawn directly), which needs no separate style file.

PORTO-CORE-068.quote: When a collection provides a render path it MUST provide at least one style telling clients how to draw it, in a format appropriate to that render path.

PORTO-CORE-069.quote: Style files are STAC assets: each style MUST be registered as a collection-level asset carrying the `style` role, alongside the data and thumbnail.

PORTO-CORE-070.quote: when a collection provides more than one style, exactly one style asset MUST carry both `style` and `default` in its `roles`.

PORTO-CORE-071.quote: A collection holding multiple raster scenes MUST model each scene as an item carrying its COG as an item-level asset; scene COGs MUST NOT be listed as collection-level assets.

PORTO-CORE-072.quote: A collection holding a single COG follows the single-file rule above: it MUST expose that COG as a collection-level asset with no item directory (see [Raster](formats.md#raster)).

PORTO-CORE-073.quote: A validator MUST probe the servers that host the publisher's metadata and asset files. It MUST NOT require third-party servers to meet these requirements for upstream copies.

PORTO-CORE-074.quote: A catalog, collection, or item MAY include a logo link with `rel: "icon"`.

PORTO-CORE-075.quote: An `icon` link MUST declare a `type`, and that type MUST be one of `image/apng`, `image/avif`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/svg+xml`, or `image/webp`.

PORTO-CORE-077.quote: The `href` SHOULD be relative, which keeps the catalog portable for the reason [Links](#links) gives.

PORTO-CORE-078.quote: A catalog or collection with twenty or more children SHOULD organize them into subcatalogs, thematic or otherwise, so users can browse the data.

PORTO-CORE-079.quote: A catalog MAY publish one STAC object tree for each language. The root catalog links to each translated root with an `alternate` link, as defined by the STAC [Language](https://github.com/stac-extensions/language) extension.

PORTO-CORE-080.quote: A translated tree represents the same catalog in another language. It is not part of the containment tree. A catalog MUST NOT link to a translated root with `child` or `item`. Each language tree has its own root catalog. That root has no `parent` link. Every `root` link in the tree points to that root catalog. Equivalent objects keep the same ID across language trees. A validator MUST treat a translated root as the start of a separate language tree. It MUST NOT report missing containment links or duplicate IDs between language trees.

PORTO-CORE-081.quote: A catalog served over the internet from a single fixed URL SHOULD carry an absolute `self` link on its root catalog.

PORTO-CORE-082.quote: A collection MUST refer to its primary data.

PORTO-CORE-083.quote: Where items do exist, each one MUST carry at least one asset with the `data` role.

PORTO-CORE-084.quote: Additional `via` links MAY reference upstream services that supply the data, with `type` set to the media type returned by each service.

PORTO-CORE-085.quote: If an asset's `href` points to the STAC object that contains it, the publisher MUST omit `file:size` and `file:checksum` from that asset's metadata.

PORTO-CORE-086.quote: To let browsers read files directly, servers MUST allow cross-origin `GET` and `HEAD` requests for all metadata and asset files. Use `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` or an equivalent policy that permits reads.

PORTO-CORE-087.quote: If an absolute `href` uses another scheme, publishers MUST also add an HTTPS URL for the same data to the asset’s [`alternate`](https://github.com/stac-extensions/alternate-assets) field.

PORTO-CORE-088.quote: Every asset SHOULD have a `title` and a `description`.

PORTO-CORE-089.quote: A validator MAY apply the requirements of the newest version it supports, whatever version an object declares.

PORTO-FMT-001.quote: STAC allows assets in any format, but Portolan requires that every collection and item is available in a cloud-optimized format, and adds requirements on specific ones: in general GeoParquet and PMTiles for vector, COG for raster, COPC for point clouds, and Parquet for non-spatial data.

PORTO-FMT-002.quote: A mirror SHOULD also include the original data as an asset when it is directly downloadable (not just an API).

PORTO-FMT-003.quote: Catalogs SHOULD reference alternate formats of data and metadata — for example an existing ISO 19115 file referenced as an asset with the `metadata` role — though new catalogs need not pre-produce them, since tooling should make translation easy.

PORTO-FMT-004.quote: Publishers MUST provide data as [GeoParquet 1.1](https://geoparquet.org/releases/v1.1.0/), [GeoParquet 2.0](https://geoparquet.org/releases/v2.0.0/), or Parquet with native [`GEOMETRY` or `GEOGRAPHY`](https://github.com/apache/parquet-format/blob/master/Geospatial.md) logical types.

PORTO-FMT-005.quote: Files SHOULD be compressed to stay small, with `zstd` RECOMMENDED.

PORTO-FMT-006.quote: Rows MUST follow a spatial order that places nearby features near each other in the file.

PORTO-FMT-007.quote: Files MUST provide per-row-group spatial statistics so readers can skip row groups from metadata alone — either: - a GeoParquet 1.1 `bbox` covering column with Parquet min/max statistics on its leaf fields (a `bbox` column without statistics does not qualify); or - for GeoParquet 2.x / Parquet `GEOMETRY` or `GEOGRAPHY`, native `GeospatialStatistics` per geometry column chunk.

PORTO-FMT-008.quote: For GeoParquet 2.x, a covering column remains RECOMMENDED even where native statistics exist, since it adds page-level min/max stats that enable finer-grained pruning.

PORTO-FMT-009.quote: Row groups MUST hold no more than 150,000 rows.

PORTO-FMT-010.quote: A PMTiles file SHOULD be provided as the visualization derivative, web-map-optimized and range-request friendly.

PORTO-FMT-011.quote: It MUST be registered through a collection-level `rel: "pmtiles"` link per the [web-map-links](https://github.com/stac-extensions/web-map-links) extension (v1.3.0): type `application/vnd.pmtiles`, a `pmtiles:layers` array of default-visible layers, with the extension's v1.3.0 schema declared in `stac_extensions`.

PORTO-FMT-012.quote: The `pmtiles:layers` array MUST be non-empty; an empty list leaves a client with nothing to display.

PORTO-FMT-013.quote: when a provider intends the PMTiles file as a genuine distribution format of the data, it MAY additionally be registered as a collection-level asset, and the link and the asset then coexist.

PORTO-FMT-014.quote: When PMTiles are provided, the collection MUST include at least one visualization style as a standalone STAC asset with the `["style"]` role, registered per [Visualization Styles](core.md#visualization-styles).

PORTO-FMT-015.quote: For PMTiles the style is a MapLibre GL style file (MapLibre GL style spec v8) in a `styles/` subdirectory, with media type `application/vnd.mapbox.style+json`, a complete, self-contained JSON loadable directly by MapLibre GL JS.

PORTO-FMT-018.quote: For spatial schemes (`kdtree`, `h3`, `s2`, `quadkey`, or `a5`), each file's path MUST show the area it covers, so that readers can skip files without opening them.

PORTO-FMT-019.quote: Publishers SHOULD also put the glob URL in the collection's `description`.

PORTO-FMT-021.quote: Every partition file MUST have the same Parquet schema, with the same columns, names, and types.

PORTO-FMT-022.quote: Partition files MAY be items when each partition has a clear meaning to users, such as one file per country. For schemes whose partitions mean nothing to users (such as hilbert, s2, or h3), or for hundreds of partitions, publishers SHOULD NOT create items.

PORTO-FMT-023.quote: Raster data MUST be provided as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) for efficient range-request access without full download.

PORTO-FMT-024.quote: Beyond that baseline, a COG MUST conform to OGC 21-026's [Optimized GeoTIFF requirements class](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-026/21-026.html#optimized_geotiff-requirements-class) (`/req/optimized_geotiff`), which adds three requirements:

PORTO-FMT-025.quote: A raster larger than a single internal tile needs internal overviews so a reader can display it zoomed out without fetching full-resolution pixels; one that already fits within a tile is exempt, since it is its own overview. Base COG validators, including `rio cogeo validate`, treat missing overviews as a warning rather than a failure. Portolan raises this to a requirement.

PORTO-FMT-026.quote: COGs MUST include pixel statistics for rendering.

PORTO-FMT-027.quote: For each band, the file MUST include an embedded minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation.

PORTO-FMT-028.quote: Publishers MUST embed these statistics in the COG file.

PORTO-FMT-029.quote: Publishers MUST write the statistics at creation time, in the file's leading header block.

PORTO-FMT-031.quote: | Valid percent | SHOULD (MUST when the band has a nodata value) |

PORTO-FMT-032.quote: | Approximate flag (`STATISTICS_APPROXIMATE = YES`) | MUST when estimated |

PORTO-FMT-033.quote: A tabular collection MUST be distinguishable from a geospatial one so that validators and federation agents relax spatial requirements and route queries correctly.

PORTO-FMT-034.quote: Data MUST be provided as a Parquet file (`application/vnd.apache.parquet`) exposed as a collection-level asset with role `["data"]`, following the single-file collection pattern — no item directory or item JSON.

PORTO-FMT-035.quote: Where a source file is converted (e.g. a CSV), the original MAY be retained as an alternate asset under the [primary-vs-alternate](core.md#assets) rule, with the Parquet as the primary.

PORTO-FMT-036.quote: A tabular collection MUST include `extent.spatial.bbox`, as required by STAC. Use the bounds of the geographic area the table is about. The bounding box does not describe a geometry footprint. Validators MUST treat the bounding box as informational.

PORTO-FMT-037.quote: Tabular collections SHOULD populate `extent.temporal` when the data has a time dimension, and SHOULD document their columns with the STAC [table](https://github.com/stac-extensions/table) extension (`table:columns` with names, types, and descriptions).

PORTO-FMT-038.quote: When geometry and attributes live in separate files (e.g. census geometries joined to a demographics table), the metadata MUST document the join columns explicitly in the README and MUST include a working code example showing how to join them.

PORTO-FMT-039.quote: Point cloud support is not yet implemented; when complete, data MUST be provided as Cloud-Optimized Point Cloud (COPC).

PORTO-FMT-040.quote: A raster collection that models scenes as items SHOULD also publish a [stac-geoparquet](https://github.com/stac-utils/stac-geoparquet) item mirror at `items.parquet` in the collection root.

PORTO-FMT-041.quote: A published item mirror MUST be registered as a collection-level asset carrying media type `application/vnd.apache.parquet` and the role `collection-mirror`

PORTO-FMT-042.quote: An item mirror is a derived Parquet copy and MUST exactly reproduce the collection's items at publication time: one row per item, with every row containing that item's fields.

PORTO-FMT-043.quote: The GeoParquet requirements above apply to item mirrors exactly as they apply to vector datasets. Rows MUST be spatially ordered, the file MUST include per-row-group spatial statistics, and row groups MUST contain no more than 150,000 rows.

PORTO-FMT-045.quote: A validator MUST apply the format requirements in this document to the catalog's own cloud-native assets and MUST NOT fail an asset for its format because it carries the `source` role.

PORTO-FMT-046.quote: A vector collection SHOULD document its columns with the STAC [table](https://github.com/stac-extensions/table) extension, carrying `table:columns` with names, types, and descriptions on the collection itself.

PORTO-FMT-047.quote: An item that carries a GeoParquet data asset, as when partition files are modeled as items, SHOULD carry the same field in its `properties`.

PORTO-FMT-048.quote: A collection whose data assets describe differing schemas MAY declare `table:columns` per asset instead.

PORTO-FMT-049.quote: A classified raster SHOULD describe these classes with `classification:classes` from the STAC [classification extension](https://github.com/stac-extensions/classification).

PORTO-FMT-050.quote: For single-band rasters, the list of classes MUST accompany the data asset. For multi-band rasters, it MUST accompany the band it describes, in the STAC 1.1 `bands` array of the data asset.

PORTO-FMT-051.quote: A collection that models scenes as items SHOULD also put the list of classes in the same place on its `item_assets` definition, so that clients can render legends without needing to open the item itself.

PORTO-FMT-052.quote: In addition to the `value`, `name`, and optional `color_hint` defined by the STAC classification extension, publishers MUST also include a human-readable `title` for every class.

PORTO-FMT-054.quote: When a classified band has a color table, the `color_hint` for each class SHOULD correspond to the red, green, and blue components of the color table entry for that class value.

PORTO-FMT-055.quote: Software that reads the catalog SHOULD draw the band based on the color table when the two differ.

PORTO-FMT-056.quote: Tools that generate the metadata MAY set a missing `color_hint` from the color table.

PORTO-FMT-057.quote: A class MUST be marked `nodata: true` if and only if its `value` equals the `nodata` value of the asset or band that has the list of classes.

PORTO-FMT-058.quote: Clients SHOULD render that class as transparent and SHOULD exclude it from the legend.

PORTO-FMT-059.quote: Continuous rasters, whose pixels are measurements such as elevation, SHOULD NOT include `classification:classes`.

PORTO-FMT-062.quote: A PMTiles asset MUST meet both conditions: - The asset has the `visual` role. - The asset belongs to a collection that references the GeoParquet data used to create the PMTiles file. Use an asset with the `data` role or `partition:glob` for the GeoParquet reference.

PORTO-FMT-063.quote: Embedded statistics MUST describe the full-resolution pixels stored in each band.

PORTO-FMT-064.quote: Because clients can't list files from a relative path or an `http://` or `https://` URL, `partition:glob` MUST be an absolute URL with a scheme that supports listing.

PORTO-FMT-065.quote: Its `href` MUST NOT contain `*` or `[`. It MAY include a query string.

PORTO-FMT-066.quote: For other S3-compatible services, such as Cloudflare R2 or MinIO, publishers SHOULD add a `storage:schemes` entry from the [STAC Storage Extension](https://github.com/stac-extensions/storage) v2.0.0.

PORTO-FMT-067.quote: Collections of multiple rasters (i.e., two or more) that share the same bands and belong to the same time period, but together cover an area much larger than that of any individual item, SHOULD provide an overview COG.

PORTO-FMT-068.quote: The overview SHOULD be an 8-bit RGB image, with an optional alpha band.

PORTO-FMT-069.quote: It SHOULD use a projection that suits web maps, such as Web Mercator (EPSG:3857).

PORTO-FMT-070.quote: Collections with mosaics for several time periods SHOULD provide an overview for at least the most recent mosaic.

PORTO-FMT-071.quote: They MAY provide an overview for each of the other periods.

PORTO-FMT-072.quote: Each overview asset SHOULD have a `datetime`, or a `start_datetime` and `end_datetime`, so clients can match it to its items.

PORTO-FMT-073.quote: For satellite and aerial imagery, publishers SHOULD declare nodata, or include an alpha band, in each scene, so that clients don't draw empty pixels as black.

PORTO-FMT-074.quote: Publishers SHOULD also use each scene's valid-data footprint as its item geometry.

PORTO-FMT-075.quote: Publishers SHOULD use `s3://`, `gs://`, or `az://`, which DuckDB, GDAL, and fsspec all support.

PORTO-FMT-077.quote: Every entry in `table:columns` SHOULD include a `description`.

PORTO-FMT-078.quote: When the dataset is a mirror and no descriptions are available for the columns, this SHOULD be noted in the collection's `README.md`.

PORTO-FMT-079.quote: Publishers SHOULD NOT include placeholder descriptions.

PORTO-FMT-080.quote: Publishers SHOULD use GeoParquet 2.0 when their tools can write it.

PORTO-FMT-081.quote: A file without a `geo` key SHOULD give the CRS of each geometry column as inline PROJJSON or a `projjson:<key>` reference in the native `crs` field.

PORTO-FMT-082.quote: Publishers SHOULD follow the [Best Practices for Distributing GeoParquet](https://guide.cloudnativegeo.org/geoparquet/) so readers can query the data without a server.

PORTO-ZARR-001.quote: A store MUST be Zarr v3.

PORTO-ZARR-002.quote: It MUST declare these conventions in `zarr_conventions` and conform to them:

PORTO-ZARR-003.quote: The store MUST be served over `https`, with an `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header that permits cross-origin reads.

PORTO-ZARR-004.quote: The STAC asset MUST follow the [asset organization](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-best-practices/blob/main/best-practices-zarr.md#asset-organization) rules of the STAC Zarr Best Practices, with media type `application/vnd.zarr; version=3`.

PORTO-ZARR-005.quote: An `s3://` href MAY be given beside the `https` one.

PORTO-ZARR-006.quote: Every renderable array MUST have an affine [`spatial:transform`](https://github.com/zarr-conventions/spatial#spatialtransform).

PORTO-ZARR-007.quote: The spatial axes MUST be the last two dimensions of every renderable array, Y before X.

PORTO-ZARR-008.quote: Arrays MUST be stored row-major (C order).

PORTO-ZARR-011.quote: A store whose finest level needs more than 4 chunks to cover its full extent MUST provide a multiscale pyramid.

PORTO-ZARR-012.quote: The coarsest level MUST fit in 4 chunks or fewer.

PORTO-ZARR-014.quote: Levels SHOULD step by a factor of 2.

PORTO-ZARR-015.quote: An append to a pyramided store MUST target the level-0 group, not the store root.

PORTO-ZARR-016.quote: A store with more than one data variable MUST declare `cube:variables`

PORTO-ZARR-017.quote: Every renderable array MUST carry at least one of:

PORTO-ZARR-018.quote: A renderable array SHOULD declare `nodata` on its `bands` entry.

PORTO-ZARR-019.quote: A store with partial coverage SHOULD carry an alpha band instead.

PORTO-ZARR-020.quote: A store MUST NOT require a client to read more than 8 samples for every sample it draws, for one timestep at full resolution.

PORTO-ZARR-021.quote: Non-spatial dimensions SHOULD have a chunk length of 1.

PORTO-ZARR-022.quote: A store chunked for time-series access SHOULD be published beside a display-chunked copy.

PORTO-ZARR-023.quote: Chunks SHOULD be 256 to 1024 samples on X and Y.

PORTO-ZARR-024.quote: A shard MAY be larger on X and Y.

PORTO-ZARR-025.quote: A shard MUST NOT span the non-spatial dimensions by a product of more than 8.

PORTO-ZARR-026.quote: Every codec in the chain SHOULD have a JavaScript implementation.
